h1: The 5 Best Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Sets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ergonomic Keyboard & Mouse: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best ergonomic keyboard and mouse options of 2026, separating true split layouts from combos that only claim comfort.
summary: The Logitech Wave Keys is our best overall because its wave-curved deck and cushioned palm rest deliver real ergonomic benefit in a compact keyboard. The Logitech Ergo K860 is the most serious split design, the Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the cheap true split, and two budget combos give a matched keyboard and mouse with only mild shaping.
intro: Most keyboard and mouse sets sold as ergonomic are not. A flat keyboard with a slightly contoured mouse and the word ergonomic on the box does almost nothing for wrist angle, and several well-known combos do not even claim it. Shoppers pay for a matched set and a label when the part that actually matters is the keyboard layout and the mouse shape.

We reviewed five options and deliberately dropped three well-known standard Logitech combos because their own listings describe a flat layout and unshaped mouse. The five that remain are ranked on paper by layout, palm support, connectivity and price tier, and the list is clear about which picks are keyboards only and which include a mouse.

products.name: Logitech Wave Keys Wireless Ergonomic Keyboard - Graphite
products.verdict: The keyboard that is actually ergonomic, in a compact body.
products.description:
The Wave Keys uses a wave-curved key deck on a single-piece frame with a rocking cushioned palm rest. It pairs over Bluetooth or a USB receiver, has a compact footprint and comes in graphite. Expect it in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It ranks first because the curved deck and palm rest change wrist posture without a steep learning curve. The K860 below is a more serious ergonomic design, but it takes more adjustment and costs more.

It suits most office workers. The caveat is that it is a keyboard only, so you need a separate mouse.
products.idealFor: Office workers wanting a real ergonomic upgrade without a steep learning curve.
products.skipIf: You want a matched keyboard and mouse in one box.

products.name: Logitech Ergo K860 Wireless Ergonomic Split Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.verdict: The most ergonomically serious keyboard here, with a true split layout.
products.description:
The Ergo K860 has a true split key layout, a full-width memory foam palm rest, reverse tilt to keep wrists more neutral, and Bluetooth for up to three devices. A Logi Bolt USB receiver is included. That puts it in the $100-200 price tier.

It ranks second because it is the most ergonomically advanced option, but the split layout needs some adjustment time and it costs the most. The Wave Keys is the easier switch.

It suits heavy typists with wrist discomfort. The caveat is that you will want a vertical mouse.
products.idealFor: Heavy typists who want the most ergonomic layout.
products.skipIf: You want a quick, easy switch.

products.name: Perixx PERIBOARD-512B Wired Ergonomic Keyboard
products.verdict: A genuine split layout for the lowest price among true ergonomic boards.
products.description:
The PERIBOARD-512B has a genuine split key layout, a molded plastic wrist rest, a wired USB connection, a Windows-specific shortcut key row and a natural typing angle. Expect it in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It ranks third because it gives the true split of the K860 for far less, but it is wired and has a plain plastic wrist rest instead of memory foam.

It suits budget buyers on Windows. The caveat is that it is not wireless and is a keyboard only.
products.idealFor: Budget Windows users wanting a true split.
products.skipIf: You want wireless or Mac layout.

products.name: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full Size Silent Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse
products.verdict: A real keyboard and mouse pair with a modest ergonomic curve and quiet keys.
products.description:
This combo has a mildly curved full-size key layout, a standard sculpted mouse (not vertical), a single 2.4G USB receiver for both devices and quiet key switches. A long battery life is claimed. It sits in the under $25 bracket.

It ranks fourth because it is the only genuinely matched set that offers any curve, but the benefit is modest next to the Wave Keys. It costs a fraction as much.

It suits budget buyers who want a matched set. The caveat is that the ergonomic gain is small.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a matched, quiet set.

products.name: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, 2.4G Full Size Silent Keyboard (Avocado Green)
products.verdict: The same budget matched-set idea in a distinctive color.
products.description:
This combo has a mildly curved full-size key layout, a 3-level DPI adjustable mouse, a single 2.4G USB receiver and an Fn multimedia key row in an Avocado Green colorway. It sits in the under $25 bracket.

It ranks fifth because its curve is as mild as the other combo's and its listing does not highlight silent switches the way the pick above does. The adjustable DPI mouse is its extra.

It suits buyers who want a color-matched desk. The caveat is that ergonomic benefit is modest.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a color-matched budget set.

whatMatters.factor: Split versus wave versus mild curve
whatMatters.detail: A true split divides the keys into two halves to reduce wrist angle. A wave curves the key deck gently, and a mild curve barely changes the layout. Check the listing for the phrase split and look at the pictures, not just the word ergonomic.
A cushioned or memory foam rest supports your wrists during long typing. A hard plastic rest adds height with less comfort. Look for the material named on the listing and for a full-width rest.
Matched sets are convenient but the mouse usually has little ergonomic shaping. Ergonomic keyboards are often sold alone. Check whether a mouse is included before assuming it.

Wired keyboards never need charging and have no lag, while wireless gives a cleaner desk. Bluetooth adds multi-device pairing and a USB receiver adds a port use. Choose based on whether you switch devices.
Split layouts can slow typing for days or weeks as your hands adjust. Gentle curves are easier. Plan on a short adjustment period and check the return window.

howToChoose.intro: How much you type each day decides how aggressive an ergonomic layout you need.

rows: 6 or more hours or wrist pain

cards.label: Split layout
cards.text: Two separated halves reduce wrist angle the most but need adjustment time. Picks here: the Logitech Ergo K860 and Perixx PERIBOARD-512B.

cards.label: Wave layout
cards.text: A curved single deck gives gentle support with almost no learning curve. Picks here: the Logitech Wave Keys and the mildly curved combos.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to a wave layout unless wrist pain is already a problem.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A cushioned palm rest, easy Bluetooth switching between laptop and desktop and a layout you can adapt to in a few days.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Logitech Wave Keys has a cushioned rocking palm rest and Bluetooth, while the Ergo K860 pairs with up to three devices.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You type for hours or already feel wrist strain, where the Logitech Ergo K860 earns its tier with a true split and memory foam.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You type lightly and want a matched set, where either budget combo is enough.

faq.q: Do these come with a mouse?
faq.a: Only the two budget combos include one. The Wave Keys, Ergo K860 and PERIBOARD are keyboards only. Pair them with a mouse separately.

faq.q: What is the biggest ergonomic set mistake?
faq.a: Trusting the word ergonomic on a flat combo. The keyboard layout and mouse shape matter. We left out standard flat combos for this reason.

faq.q: Is the K860 worth it over the Wave Keys?
faq.a: If you have wrist pain or type all day, yes. For most people the Wave Keys gives enough benefit for less. The split needs more adjustment.

faq.q: How do I adapt to a split keyboard?
faq.a: Expect a slower typing speed for the first week and practice with the hand positions. Raise the palm rest height gradually. Keep wrists straight.

faq.q: How do I maintain an ergonomic keyboard?
faq.a: Wipe the keys and palm rest regularly and replace batteries on wireless models. Dust under keys with compressed air. Check the receiver connection if lag appears.

faq.q: Will these work with a Mac?
faq.a: Check the listing for OS support. The PERIBOARD has a Windows-specific shortcut row. Bluetooth keyboards generally pair, but key labels may differ.

finalTake: The Logitech Wave Keys is the best ergonomic option for most people because it delivers real wrist support with almost no learning curve. The Logitech Ergo K860 is the pick for heavy typists, and the Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the budget true split. If you want a simple matched set, either budget combo works, but expect only modest ergonomics.
